column1: # Tier-D3 cases: <layout>TAB<keys>[TABmode]. Expectations are derived at run
# time from hunmin-sim --trace (tier A is the single source of truth).
# mode column: empty = COMMIT-only (the default, and the stronger claim -- the
# client sees exactly what the engine committed). "stream" = also expect the
# characters for keys the engine DECLINED, i.e. what the input method forwarded
# back to the client. Needed only for pass-through keys, which is why space
# used to be excluded from this file entirely.
# Before 2026-10-09 the rule here was "no pass-through keys, so the XIM COMMIT
# stream equals the sim commit stream". That was not a property of the design;
# it was the XIM harness having no forward_event callback, so dkit discarded
# every key fcitx5 handed back and a pass-through key could not be seen at all.
# See the comment block above on_forward() in xim-harness.c.
dubeolsik
sin3-p2
sin3-p2
# The disputed case: space must end the composition (COMMIT) and still arrive
# as a character (FORWARD). Under dubeolsik `dkssuds ` commits 안, 녕 and then
# ㄴ, with the space itself declined by the engine.
dubeolsik
# Cultural text complex scenarios -- full sentences compose correctly.
# Keys generated by tools/sin3p2-ksgen.py (BFS over the engine automaton;
# shortest keystroke per syllable, joined). Do not hand-edit: a keystroke
# typed by guesswork does not survive tier A. Regenerate with, e.g.:
#   python3 tools/sin3p2-ksgen.py --text-file <text> --layout dubeolsik \
#       --max-len 4 --out <out.json>
# then join the per-syllable keystrokes in text order. Space is included as a
# key so the stream mode also proves the engine declines it (FORWARD), not
# just that the syllables commit.
# dubeolsik 애국가 1절: "동해물과 백두산이 마르고 닳도록 하느님이 보우하사 우리나라 만세"
dubeolsik
